message.content:
**Uno – Quick Overview** | What | How it works | |------|--------------| | **Goal** | Be the first player to score 500 points (or agree on a different target). Points are earned by being the first to finish each round. | | **Setup** | • Shuffle the Uno deck (108 cards).
• Deal 7 cards to each player.
• Place the remaining cards face‑down as the draw pile.
• Flip the top card of the draw pile to start the discard pile. | | **Turn order** | Players take turns clockwise (unless a reverse card is played). | | **Playing a card** | On your turn you may play one card from your hand that matches the discard pile’s **color**, **number**, or **symbol**. If you cannot play, you must draw a card. | | **Special cards** | • **Skip** – next player loses a turn.
• **Reverse** – changes direction of play.
• **Draw Two** – next player draws two cards and loses a turn.
• **Wild** – you choose the new color.
• **Wild Draw Four** – you choose the new color; next player draws four cards and loses a turn (must be challenged if you suspect you could have played a matching card). | | **Winning a round** | When a player discards their last card, they shout “Uno!” if they have one card left. If they forget, the next player must draw two penalty cards. | | **Scoring** | The winner of the round scores points equal to the sum of all cards left in opponents’ hands: numbers = face value, Skip/Reverse/Draw Two = 20, Wild/Wild Draw Four = 50. | | **Game end** | First player to reach the agreed‑upon point total wins the game. | **Key Tips** 1. Keep track of the current color and number so you can anticipate opponents’ moves. 2. Use Wild cards strategically to change the color when you’re stuck. 3. Challenge a Wild Draw Four only if you’re sure the player could have played a matching card; otherwise you’ll have to draw four cards yourself. That’s the core of Uno—simple to learn, but with enough strategy to keep it fun!
